$readme: The marginalia: the philosophy map, and the quote and equation of the day (same lists and daily pick as the profile README).
thinkers: in rough chronological order. native is the name in the thinker's own tongue; lang is grc | la | de | en (de is set in fraktur).
influences: [reader-of, reader] pairs, i.e. [plato, aristotle] means aristotle read plato.
quotes: Essentially, all models are wrong, but some are useful.
The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution.
We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
Mathematics is the art of giving the same name to different things.
What I cannot create, I do not understand.
The universe is not only queerer than we suppose, but queerer than we can suppose.
Far better an approximate answer to the right question, which is often vague, than an exact answer to the wrong question, which can always be made precise.
The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers.
It is a capital mistake to theorize before one has data.
If you torture the data long enough, it will confess.
He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
The map is not the territory.
The unexamined life is not worth living.
If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
The theory of probabilities is at bottom nothing but common sense reduced to calculus.
We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
The Cosmos is all that is or ever was or ever will be.
Nature uses only the longest threads to weave her patterns, so that each small piece of her fabric reveals the organization of the entire tapestry.
Biology is the study of complicated things that give the appearance of having been designed for a purpose.
Not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted.
The greatest value of a picture is when it forces us to notice what we never expected to see.
Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.
The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious.
Equipped with his five senses, man explores the universe around him and calls the adventure Science.
My formula for greatness in a human being is amor fati.
